title: Automated ASPECTS scoring for acute ischemic stroke
summary: Assist clinicians by calculating ASPECTS from brain imaging and presenting an explainable result.
description:
Clinical Motivation

In acute stroke, time is brain. Clinicians must decide within a narrow window whether a patient qualifies for thrombolysis or thrombectomy, and that decision hinges partly on ASPECTS (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score), a 10-point score radiologists compute manually under time pressure from a non-contrast CT (NCCT). Each of 10 predefined regions in the middle-cerebral-artery territory - caudate, lentiform nucleus, insula, internal capsule, and M1-M6 - is inspected for early ischemic change; one point is deducted per affected region. The process is subjective, reader-dependent, and slow at exactly the moment speed matters most.

The Challenge

Build an end-to-end system that estimates ASPECTS from an NCCT head scan: detect early ischemic change such as loss of grey-white differentiation or subtle hypodensity, localize it to the correct ASPECTS regions, and output a 0-10 score. A system that does one objective well but ignores the other is incomplete.

Objective 1 - Ischemic Change Detection (the ML core)

On NCCT, detect and segment areas of early ischemic change. The signal may be only a few Hounsfield units rather than a bright bleed. Hemispheric symmetry is the strongest cue because the healthy contralateral side is a built-in reference. Left-right symmetry analysis and contralateral density comparison are encouraged, and a rule-based plus ML hybrid is legitimate.

Objective 2 - ASPECTS Region Localization and Scoring

Map the 10 ASPECTS regions onto the patient scan and derive the score. Pre-built ASPECTS region atlases in standard space may be used. The atlas must be registered robustly onto each native NCCT despite varying head tilt, slice thickness, and skull stripping, because a naive rigid fit can misassign regions. Keep final scoring rule-based and explainable by comparing per-region HU values with the contralateral side. Registration toolkits may include ANTs, elastix, SimpleITK, or a learned method such as VoxelMorph.

The Interface Between Them (where systems break)

The two objectives must connect: detected change has to land in the correct region after registration. Consider the shared coordinate frame, how registration error propagates into wrong region assignments, and how a small detection near a region boundary is handled.

Datasets

APIS (primary): a public paired NCCT and ADC-MRI dataset for acute ischemic stroke, with NCCT lesion labels derived from MRI. It contains approximately 60 training pairs and 36 test pairs and is available by registration. AISD (secondary) contains 397 NCCT scans with DWI-confirmed lesion masks, including 345 training and 52 test scans. ISLES 2018 is CT-perfusion and ISLES 2022 is MRI-only; use them only as reference material because neither provides NCCT ASPECTS labels.

ASPECTS Atlas and Registration Resources (for Objective 2)

An NCCT ASPECTS atlas with 10 labeled regions, atlas files on Figshare, the MIPLAB elderly NCCT/FLAIR atlas, a whole-brain stroke-population CT-MRI atlas, and published atlas-based scoring methods may be used as registration and validation resources.

Deliverables

A pipeline that takes an NCCT volume and returns: (a) a segmentation or heatmap of detected ischemic change, (b) a per-region ischemic-change flag across the 10 ASPECTS regions, and (c) an overall ASPECTS score. Include a visualization overlaying both the detected change and the 10 region boundaries on the CT.

title: Build an AI powered windshield installation guidance system
summary: Using cameras and computer vision algorithms, the system will identify the windshield area and display predefined pressure application points on the windshield or on the monitor or augmented display. Operators will be guided to sequentially apply pressure (with adequate pressure) at each designated location. The system will track completion of all required points and provide immediate confirmation once the standard process has been followed correctly
description:
Problem Context

The windshield installation process is performed manually on the vehicle assembly line. Operators must apply pressure across the windshield according to defined standard operating procedures for proper sealing and adhesion. Missed or incorrectly applied pressure can result in inconsistent fitment, loose installation, water leakage, noise or vibration issues, and increased rework.

Problem Statement 

Build an AI powered Windshield Installation Guidance System that provides operators with real-time visual feedback during the fitment process.Using cameras and computer vision algorithms, the system will identify the windshield area and display predefined pressure application points on the windshield or on the monitor or augmented display. Operators will be guided to sequentially apply pressure(with adequate pressure) at each designated location. The system will track completion of all required points and provide immediate confirmation once the standard process has been followed correctly.

What You May Build

a) A Computer Vision-powered solution that identifies the windshield area in real time and guides operators through predefined pressure application points during installation. The system verifies that all required zones are pressed according to standard operating procedures, ensuring consistent fitment quality and reducing operator-dependent variations.

b)An intelligent vision system that monitors the windshield installation process and validates whether pressure has been applied at every critical bonding location. The engine detects missed points, incomplete sequences, or incorrect installation patterns and provides immediate corrective feedback before the vehicle moves to the next station.

c)An AI agent that continuously analyses installation data, operator actions, and fitment compliance records to identify recurring quality issues, process deviations, and training needs. The agent provides actionable insights to improve first-pass yield and reduce warranty claims.

Suggested Technical Stack

Computer vision
Real-time tracking system
Agentic AI or multi-agent systems
Web application

title: Build an AI-Powered assembly inspection system
summary: Verify manufacturing assembly quality with computer vision, AI, and optional wearable AR.
description:
Problem Context

In manufacturing environments, assembly quality verification is often dependent on manual visual inspections to ensure that wiring assemblies, connectors, fasteners, clips, and other components are installed according to prescribed standards. These inspections require operators to verify routing paths, fastening locations, component positioning. While manual inspection remains widely used, it is susceptible to human error, inspection variability, fatigue, and inconsistency across shifts. Missed defects such as incorrect routing, unsecured components, missing fasteners, or unintended contact between assemblies can lead to quality concerns, increased rework, production delays, warranty costs, and reduced product reliability.

Problem Statement

Build an AI-Powered Assembly Inspection System that combines Computer Vision, Artificial Intelligence, and Wearable AR devices(optional) to automate assembly verification and quality inspection processes. Using real-time image analysis, AI models compare live assembly conditions against approved digital standards to identify deviations such as incorrect routing, missing fastening elements, improper component positioning, or potential interference risks. Inspection results are visualized through augmented reality overlays, enabling operators and inspectors to instantly identify and resolve issues within their field of view.The system provides real-time guidance, automated defect detection, digital traceability, and standardized inspection processes, helping manufacturers improve quality assurance and operational efficiency.

What You May Build

a)A Computer Vision-based inspection solution capable of analysing assembly conditions in real time and detecting deviations from approved assembly standards, including routing errors, missing components, and incorrect positioning.

b)An AI-powered quality verification engine that compares live production images with digital reference models and automatically identifies defects, potential interference conditions before products move to subsequent manufacturing stages.

c)An Augmented Reality guidance system that overlays inspection results, assembly instructions, and defect locations directly onto physical components through wearable smart glasses, enabling hands-free quality verification.

d)An AI Agent that continuously analyses inspection records, defect trends, production data, and operator performance to identify recurring quality issues, predict defect-prone areas, and recommend process improvements.

e)A digital traceability platform that records inspection outcomes, defect classifications, images, compliance metrics, and corrective actions to create a comprehensive quality history for every manufactured unit.

Suggested Technical Stack

Computer vision
Real-time tracking system
Agentic AI or multi-agent systems
Web or mobile application
3D modelling
AR/VR

title: Build an AI-Powered manufacturing operations assistant
summary: Help factory teams understand constraints, validate plans, detect risks, and keep production moving.
description:
Problem Context

Modern manufacturing plants generate large amounts of real-time information related to material shortages, inventory availability, production flow, and operational constraints. Much of this information is spread across emails, messages, sensors, and different software systems.Today, production planners must manually monitor these inputs, validate production schedules, identify potential bottlenecks, manage exceptions, and take corrective actions when disruptions occur. This process is time-consuming, reactive, and heavily dependent on human expertise.As industries move towards smart factories, there is a need for intelligent systems that can continuously monitor operations, predict problems before they happen, and help maintain smooth production flow with minimal human intervention.

Problem Statement

Build an AI-Powered Manufacturing Operations Assistant that can monitor real-time factory data, understand operational constraints, validate production plans, detect risks, and recommend corrective actions to keep production running smoothly.The solution should use AI agents to collect information from multiple sources, analyse current factory conditions, identify potential issues such as material shortages or production bottlenecks, and provide actionable recommendations to planners and operators.The system should help manufacturers make faster decisions, reduce manual effort, improve production efficiency, and increase overall operational reliability.

What You May Build

a)An AI agent that automatically gathers and understands information from emails, chats, reports, or factory systems and converts it into structured operational insights.
b)An intelligent planning assistant that validates production schedules and identifies potential risks before execution.
c)A predictive monitoring system that detects bottlenecks, congestion, shortages, or flow disruptions before they affect production.
dA recommendation engine that suggests corrective actions and recovery plans when operational issues are detected.
e)An autonomous decision-support platform that combines multiple AI agents to monitor, analyse, and optimize factory operations in real time.

Suggested Technical Stack

Generative AI and LLMs
Agentic AI or multi-agent systems
Machine learning and predictive analysis
Natural language processing (NLP)
